title: Local invariance of derived extension to constant coefficients
statement: Let i:Y→X be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], R a commutative ring sheaf on X_proet, B an arbitrary commutative ring, φ:R→constant(B), U an object of Y_proet, and K,K′ objects of D(R-modules). Use the ordinary derived scalar extension and the actual-ring local restriction of [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. Suppose sfbLocalRestriction i R U K ≅ sfbLocalRestriction i R U K′. Define residue(M) by applying fixed B-scalar restriction termwise to a localization representative of completedAdicDerivedChange X φ M and then localizing. With L the fixed B-scalar inverse image along i followed by slice restriction to U, there is an isomorphism D(L)(residue(K)) ≅ D(L)(residue(K′)). No adic, completeness, boundedness, immersion, finite-generation or perfectness assumption is required.

source.place: lemma-derived-base-change (Tag 06YY), lemma-pullback-K-flat (Tag 0G7E), lemma-pullback-tensor-product, and lemma-restriction-K-flat (Tag 0E8K); constant-ring action normalized by the constant-sheaf inverse-image comparison.

proof.text: Identify sfbLocalRestriction with the derived exact composite H of actual-ring inverse image and slice restriction. Cancel identity-coefficient extension using uniqueness of left adjoints and the identity restriction isomorphism; compose the exact localization factor and representative isomorphisms.

Use the ordinary B-linear natural tensor comparison between global scalar extension followed by fixed-scalar local restriction and H followed by scalar extension on the slice and fixed scalars there. Fixed scalar restriction is exact because it retains the underlying abelian sheaf.

Resolve every complex by a flat-term K-flat complex. Algebraic inverse image preserves K-flatness of these complexes by the existing pullback computation with identity coefficient extension; slice restriction preserves K-flatness. The two scalar-extension counits are thus invertible on the resolving class. Whisker these counits by the exact functors and descend their conjugate ordinary comparison through the fully faithful restriction to resolving representatives.

Map the supplied local isomorphism by the derived scalar-extension functor on the slice followed by exact fixed scalar restriction. Conjugate by the descended comparison and by the exact localization-representative identifications of residue. This yields the required fixed-B derived isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YY, 0G7E and 0E8K; resolving-class descent of the ordinary B-linear tensor comparison, written in Lean by Z7.

lean.statement:
theorem proEtaleLocalScalarDerivedIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X)
    {R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}}
    (B : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing B]
    (φ : R ⟶ (constantSheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj
      (CommRingCat.of B))
    (U : Y.ProEt) (K K' : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X R))
    (e : sfbLocalRestriction i R U K ≅ sfbLocalRestriction i R U K') :
    let L := ProEtale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) i ⋙
      (ProEt.topology Y).overPullback (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) U
    letI : L.Additive := Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products L
    let F := sfbFixedScalarRestriction X B
    let residue := fun M : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X R) ↦
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.objPreimage ((completedAdicDerivedChange X φ).obj M)))
    Nonempty (L.mapDerivedCategory.obj (residue K) ≅
      L.mapDerivedCategory.obj (residue K'))
